item.title: A Treasure Chest for (media) Pirates
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Normal, but with "Notable Files" log.

Elevator Pitch: An anomaly where filesharing sites and FTP servers spontaneously obtain all pieces of media, even lost media with no evidence for its existence.

Central Narrative: Upon the first manifestation of the anomaly on ftp://[REDACTED], The Foundation, upon discovering mountains of classified material, and world governments, upon discovering mountains of illegal content, collaborate to shut down sites affected by SCP-XXXX. One server is archived by the Foundation, and contains the presumably infinite (yet 100TB in size) archive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Notable content is recorded on a log by Information Researcher Jones. Throughout the logs, he documents his experiences and how his mental state is affected from seeing some of the more disturbing content in the archive.

Additional Notes: The concept of this is essentially "What if the Foundation was responsible for shutting down so many filesharing sites?".

item.title: Re: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
1) It's not THAT family-friendly when her mere image causes violence in men. Also, don't introduce it as a "modern take" or "gender-bending"; it's just marketing copy that turns off a lot of people.

If that's all your story has going for it, then it needs something else.

2) I'm honestly interested in how they held the interviews; that alone would be interesting to see. I'm thinking it would be via text-only, making it sort of interesting.

3) That said. you need to seriously build this up somehow. As it stands right now it's probably better in the Tales section than as a straight article. This relies solely on its narrative elements to be interesting, rather than on the anomaly itself. Thus, while this is an interesting story, especially if the humor is played up, I'm not sure how "lesbian siren" would play as an article.

item.title: Dissociative Somnia Phenomenon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: YES

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch:
An event in which an individual, usually that suffers from night terrors, will experience a dissociative episode(out of body experience) by "dreaming" about dying or killing. The dreams represent with precision the death of a person close to them, who will die within the next few weeks. Attempts to prevent this fate will often result in catastrophic outcomes.

Central Narrative:
The Inevitability of death and acceptance of loss.

Hook:
It's the classic "how would you react if you knew someone that you like is going to die?". I believe this concept to be interesting enough for the small intended size of the article.

Additional notes:
I'm not a hundred percent sure there isn't anything like this on the site already. I've looked around and found nothing that's close, but if there is, please, feel free to warn me.

item.title: Re: Complete Desolation
item.content:encoded:
The obvious problem you have is that it's based on a tac-nuke; while it's always fun to go into what a tac-nuke can do, they are just unlikely to target something small enough to be taken out with one. Upgrading it just creates bigger problems. You'd do better with an epidemic or invasion, which have been known to take out towns.

It would also be harder to keep the city out of the news.

It is worth noting that experimentation would be able to determine if he is truly schizophrenic or is actually talking to ghosts; The Foundation would be able to determine that. If he truly is talking to ghosts, then The Foundation would have specialists that would love to talk to him. If he's merely schizophrenic, The Foundation getting him help would make for some interesting debates similar to whether or not he could leave the town.

Otherwise, an excellent start. It should be interesting to see where this goes.

item.title: Re: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.content:encoded:
It's an interesting idea, but limited in terms of testing (once The Foundation has a few solid tests in terms of the progression they'll likely stop). The two biggest problems are how to stop or even reset the progression, and how to actually find it.

Also, you may want to consider that just creating an SCP that's annoying is usually not enough, but has to have some sort of narrative background to it, such as where it comes from, was it designed by a group with a specific agenda in mind, or even an accident of evolution.

It's a good basic idea, but needs to be fleshed out some.

item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

First of all a big thank you also to you for taking the time and effort to give me feedback.

+ Nobody here
- Nobody still here

I wanted to make a pun, as Gestalten in German can also mean "suspicious figures" in certain contexts.
As an example:

German – Einige dubiose Gestalten schlichen um das Haus herum.
English – Some dubious crooks crept around the house.

I find this funny in the context of Nobody, because Nobody is exactly the type of person who is up to something at night and in the fog.

If they're physically separated, why are they all writing on the same page?
Like it'd make sense for a few of them to get together and write on the same page but there's like…20? of them?

I had planned to make it no more than 7, but when I counted, I came up with 13 or so. I'm going to change that.

I'm a little torn on this as a whole

I see what you mean, this is also the reason why I so urgently request feedback.

If this article survives, I will certainly write a serious tale where I develop the idea of a "Nobody gang". Just the idea that they keep their personalities after the "Noodle Incident" and the whole group tries to get along with each other is very entertaining for me.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Good Evening, all.

I'm DiamondFriday98, and I'm an aspiring fiction writer from the UK, as well as being a practising copy-writer. I am currently working on a remote placement year for a magazine company in China producing articles, proofreading and editing their English-language content. Aside from that I am studying in university on a Media Communications course.

I'm here on the SCP wiki both because the setting and entries have interested me for a long time, to destress from my usual job and recapture the joy of writing for it's own sake. I struggle with having few people close to me to show my work, or adequate motivation & formatting to keep my attention. I think the format of the SCP wiki, it's articles and whatnot will help me recapture my desire to write.

If (correct me if I'm wrong) we're supposed to answer the 'random question' in our posts, I'd say that I'm closest to Air, I tend to have a low attention span, moving from one subject/hobby to another constantly. I can strongly embrace them and then immediately evaporate, but I like to think I can always return to them.

I hope you'll all enjoy having me and we'll be able to constructively discuss each other's work and the world of the SCP wiki! And if necessary I may repost this in the upcoming month's thread as we only have about a day before December.

item.title: Re: The innate nature of things.
item.content:encoded:
Hi Thanks for the feedback. You asked some questions directly so I'm going to answer them here.

+ show block
– hide block

Is this a 'mechanism' as in like, a physical machine? or a mechanism as in an abstract process?

It's an abstract process. Because the whole environment of the universe is a product of this machine on both a physical and metaphysical level the machine can leave abstract triggers that allow you to interface with it. If you know anything about computers it's a little like an OS providing code running under it with access to system calls that can be used to request more memory and print stuff to the screen. Its like a system call embedded in reality on an abstract level.

You would use these triggers with your mind but it would be very difficult. Something only a few people can do. I'll leave the actual experience of using one of these triggers mostly up to the imagination but indicate that it's something fundamentally difficult to express in words (hence why it's such a hard skill to teach).

What's the security like here? How does it make progress harder?

This feels…like a really weird way to solve this problem

I agree. This was little bit of a throwaway line.

In my head I imagined big doors with complicated mechanical locks that take weeks to crack. Shifting hallways and an impossible to map structure. This is a tad generic though so I will probably try and develop this before my next idea draft.

Regarding the narrative being passive I'd say I agree with that. I'm going to go away and think about all of this before coming back and rewriting this document. I'm very confident that I can polish this up.

Your feedback has been indispensable and I hope you will take another look when the next version is ready.

Thanks for your time.

item.title: Complete Desolation
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A city thought to be destroyed by a tactical nuke is completely intact and functioning normally With one heat signature

Central Narrative: The heat signature is from a man that when researched can be found on file from [DATA REDACTED], Japan. He doesn’t seem aware that a nuke hit said city and lives in it agelessly

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man has been shown to be talking to unknown people in the city in trivial conversation. It is unknown whether he is talking to an anomalous affect or is a schizophrenic. However when going to place of residence he shows signs of depression, possibly showing sapience to his situation.

Additional Notes: When the man goes to the edges of the city large tremors happen around him. It is unknown if him leaving will result in his neutralization. To counteract this he is forced by the foundation to stay in the inner area of the city until more information is found.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Complete Desolation

This is a scout for some kind of extra dimensional invasion, sent here to learn every possible way humans kill things so the invading soldiers can prepare. Every time they test this machine, they are making it harder to repel this eventual invasion. However, as long as we keep testing it regularly, the invasion won’t happen, not until they’re sure they’ve seen every possible means of being killed. This is why SCP-001-EX said testing should continue indefinitely.

Optionally, the invading species are the puppies. The machine can’t repeat termination methods because they adapt immediately.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight On My Idea
item.content:encoded:
My apologies on being too vague. Allow me to try and respond to some of your concerns. (Still not very good at formatting, but I'll try)

What do these interviews/interrogations actually like…add narratively here? My concern is that they're going to be either relatively info-dumpy or relatively contentless depending on how co-operative the people being interviewed are.

I have a multitude of ideas for these interviews which (as I haven't begun writing them yet) aren't super fleshed out, but have, what I think is, a good basis.

  • A local who's fountain, one day, produced very hot water, but only once- this one is more comedic, to open the logs on a lighter note. Interviewers will try and focus the question on the fountains appearance and disappearance itself, but the interviewed man will be hyperfocused on the hot water. As these people believe, and perceive, these fountains as completely natural phenomenon, it'd be like waking up one day to your grass being a neon red, and being unable to prove it to anyone.
  • One or two individuals who have lived in the area for JUST UNDER the time it takes for the memetic effects to take hold. They will be noticably distressed and nervous, aware that something is taking place out of the ordinary, but unable to question it fully. These are more worldbuilding
  • Interview with a police chief/undecided government official of some sort. The Foundation tries to see if any of the upper-caste of society, leader of any small religious group, etc, has any connection to these fountains, but comes up empty handed, and starts to become weary on further investigation
  • A junior researcher comes across something peculiar. In one of the more isolated, backwoods properties of the township, an older man is seen praying to his fountain every Tuesday. This totally breaks the previous conception that everyone affected sees the fountains as normal. The man is interviewed and interrogated, and is identified as one of the few remaining members of the nearby Ramapough Lenape natives. He is stubborn to give information at first, but a search of his property reveals a journal which has been logging the appearances of the fountains for the past few decades.

Then, I plan to detail the log the man has written, which will give further insight into the phenomenon of this SCP. I understand the "Native American curse" concept may be somewhat overdone, not entirely sure, but I think I can take this in an interesting direction while also bringing to light some of the slights against the Ramapough Lenape.

The log will stretch back to the mid-70s/early-80s, with a preface, where the man recounts losing close family members to contaminated water and food due to a (very real) toxic waste landfill used by Ford in which affordable housing was constructed upon. Everything after that in the log, will be mostly excluded/expunged, menial information (pH testing, and marking the times the fountains appear) as to avoid massive exposition. The township he's selected to test his revenge on is a perfectly isolated, echo chamber of a community. A place where the population would hardly question, or have the dialogue to discuss, such a phenomenon, before it takes hold. An incubation chamber for a more diabolical scheme. The extent, and area of attack of this scheme, will be left to the reader, somewhat.

After holding the man for a period of one week, and maintaining testing of his fountain, Foundation researchers will notice a new presence of dangerous levels of lead contaminants. Upon release, the fountains will return to their normal state of producing clean water, but the damage is done- many residents have been killed or are seriously ill after consumption of the water. They are all, however, unable to recognize that the fountains were the cause of this.

An addendum will tie things up, from one of the interviewers, warning that further disruption of the phenomenon could be genocidal, and to focus all efforts on surveillance of the identified suspect, to avoid spread of the phenomenon out of the affected township.

you gotta give everything away here btw like if a reviewer doesn't have a full idea of what your idea actually is, it's very hard for them to judge whether it's a good idea.

I hope this cleared things up, a little. If anything is too overboard, doesn't seem to work (in your eyes), let me know. I am more than happy to rework this as much as needed, even from the ground up. I really feel like I have something here that can be informative, unsettling, and neuron-firing, without being a super scary bloody beast, or a gore fest or super powerful humanoid. If I am wrong in that feeling, please just let me know.

item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Some questions and info that might help you see the issues here, and point you down a more productive path:

Why is it a millipede? Not just in the mechanical sense, but why, for the purposes of the story, is it a millipede rather than a centipede, or a robot, or a bowl of nachos with legs? There should be a why, at least in your mental notes. If there isn't: Why is it a millipede?

Why does it attack things? Again, if there isn't a reason: Why does it attack things?

Why is it a germaphobe? (This is actually the most interesting aspect at the moment, btw. Zero sarcasm: maybe give it cleaning supplies and have it join the site cleaning crew.)

What makes this an SCP? The Foundation has loads of giant bugs in containment. What makes this one require Special containment procedures instead of "lock it up and feed it periodically"

Potentially relevant info regarding millipedes: In the early days of land-dwelling life, millipedes were some of the largest creatures on Earth, some species measuring around 2 meters. They had no known predators. Almost all species of millipede (past and present) are herbivores. Their survival mechanisms are almost entirely defensive measures- they curl up, some taste bad or excrete mildly irritating chemicals, some have bristles…it's all protection, no offense. Some of the most harmless creatures on earth, really.

'fat' is…a strange modifier for 'kick' in english; I'd probably change it to either 'big' or just…leave it unmodified? Or change it to 'I want to kick that ones ass' so it's more of a general 'beat them up' vibe

Way too many Gestalten

If they're physically separated, why are they all writing on the same page?

Like it'd make sense for a few of them to get together and write on the same page but there's like…20? of them?

Like if they started off shitposting and having fun and then gradually they all realised that this was a mistake and the arc shifted towards them trying to fix it; or perhaps if they just like…started to take it more seriously or something? Which like, the second page starts on but it feels like it might need to go further?

Then again, there's a part of me that sort of likes the idea of this being a like…collaborative log where folk can write little things from the perspective of being a nobody; though it feels like it'd quickly turn to a big shitposting spree and crash and burn if that happened so maybe not.

item.title: Re: SCP draft Crit
item.content:encoded:
(Requested to take another look at this through PM)

Alright, some things are definitely better:

  • The exploration log is now written as an exploration log, which is great!
  • The Special Containment Procedures section is more structured
  • Tone has improved in the Description section
  • There are less grammatical errors and sentence structure has been improved, which makes it easier to read (however if you want to have the whole article checked for these kinds of things, you may want to find someone more knowledgeable in that field than me)

It's alright thus far, but I've noticed a very important thing: The tone in the exploration log and other documents is very unprofessional

+ Crit on tone
- Hide crit

Alright, let's take a quote:

Researcher: Have you experienced anything yet class-D? Your heart rate is slowly gaining pace.
D-45305: Yea, I'm fine. It's just… I don't want to do this anymore. Please don't make me do this, I'm very claustro-
Researcher: Hush now, you know exactly why you are here. Don't forget it. You will comply with this mission and orders and you'll not complain. Do I make myself clear?
D-45305: (Silence)
Researcher: Do I make myself clear.
D-45305: Yes. sniff
Researcher: Good rat.

If a researcher handles a D-class in this way, they can expect a lengthy disciplinary hearing from the ethics committee. Why? Because D-class are still people, even if they are used for experiments. They aren't meant to be expendable, contrary to popular belief; D-class just means that they don't have the clearance codes for almost all files and places. Calling a test-subject, even an unwilling one, ''rat'' is highly unprofessional and unexpected from a trained Foundation researcher. It should be noted that this does not apply to the d-class themselves.

Also, I've noticed that you write the researcher like some evil maniac: he's intimidating the D-class, he's saying that the D-class isn't allowed to feel happy, etc. You should understand this: The Foundation is not evil. Even if some of their decisions are questionable, they won't abuse, hurt, or destroy unnecessarily. They even have an ethics committee to ensure that this happens. Try to keep this in mind when writing the character of the researcher.

TLDR; The Foundation is not evil, but cold and calculated. Researchers don't intimidate D-class and remain professional when conducting experiments or supervising explorations.

If you're still willing to go with an assertive researcher, I have a quick example with the previous quote:

Researcher: Have you experienced anything yet class-D? Your heart rate is slowly gaining pace.
D-45305: Yea, I'm fine. It's just… I don't want to do this anymore. Please don't make me do this, I'm very claustro-
Researcher: D-45305, please continue down the tunnel. Failure to comply will increase your sentence.
(silence)
Researcher: D-45305, do you understand?
D-45305: Yes.
Researcher: Good. Please continue down the tunnel.

Something like that. Please keep this in mind when revising your exploration log.

P.S. Here's a quote, again:

Both personnel were hypnotized at the sight of SCP-XXXX-A-2 sky which represented a neubla. The sky consistently changed in color and gases creating a mesmerizing pattern to the beat of the current song playing in SCP-XXXX-A-2. It appears to have a psychological affect causing all creatures that observe it to feel relaxed and emotional.

If a property of an SCP is discovered in an exploration log, it is best to make these kinds of observations at the end of the log. You only write the things that actually happen in the exploration; it's usually based on a recording, and a recording usually doesn't tell you that someone was mesmerized or that the SCP seemed to have a special effect on them. You can make these kinds of remarks as footnotes, or as a small section after the log titled ''note'' or something like that.

That is all! (for now) If you want me to look at something specific, just DM me.

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Romance, History

Elevator Pitch: A siren that travels the world's seas in search of someone to marry. She exposes people to auditory and visual memetic agents that will make the exposed person fall in love with her; this usually ends with the siren accidentally drowning the exposed person. Any accurate depiction of her also carries this effect. However, the memes will only work on people who identify as a woman: people who identify as male will have a violent reaction to memes. The memes aren't distributed by artistic interpretations of her.

She first appeared in 1882; she was less of a problem then because she mostly isolated herself in the middle of the Atlantic ocean, not aware of the outside world. However, with the rise of mass media and the internet, she became more of a problem to secrecy as she began patrolling closer to large population centers and started placing advertisements carrying memetic agents on the internet through anomalous and non-anomalous means.

Central Narrative: The foundation originally discovered the siren in 1882, but due to her remote location, the foundation maneuvered ships away from her position and kept her mostly uncontained. The disappearance of Natalie Wood is the first real sign that the Siren has taken more provocative actions to secure a bride. The foundation can get a hold of her and does some interviews:

  • The first goes in-depth about her history: Her familial line is dying off and she was forced into marriage. However, due to her sexuality and her failing relationship with her husband, she ran away from home in search of another bride.
  • The second has the foundation propose an alternative; she can find a bride within the foundation staff as long as she stops advertising on the internet.
  • The third is a list of multiple proposed brides, equipped with memetic dampeners, and the siren's reaction to them. One of them gets selected, and some conversations are logged. It ends on a sweet tone, the siren finally having found someone who likes her back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a wholesome article and this is mostly targeted at an audience that likes that, and it's pretty big. It also plays with the siren formula and introduces it to a modern setting. You could see it as a more family-friendly version of the original ''teenage succubus'' SCP.

item.title: Re: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
I guess I'll explain what I can about the narrative; I wasn't going to, since this is only a brief initial pitch, but hopefully you'll find this to be interesting at least. Here's the plot summary:

+ show block
– hide block

I'm hoping that the reader will interpret that by the absence of fetal tissue in the enlarged uterus and the shrunken portions of the woman's brain that regulate cognitive functions, sensory input, movement, and memory, that the fetus mutated in a way that caused it to absorb the mother's brain functions and dissolve, sinking into the legs with only the nervous system surviving, which means that the nervous system is essentially a hive mind of the mother and fetus. The mother had been wandering as a result of her brain's degradation and died in the snow, being frozen for an indiscriminate amount of time so that it would be difficult to pinpoint when she died. When the corpse thawed, the legs and lower torso forcibly pulled itself away from the upper body, confused due to its overall lack of "brain power," but with enough sense of direction (likely due to the mutation, or perhaps from the mother's prior knowledge and memory) to know approximately where the nearest village is, but never finds its way there and is instead picked up by the foundation when villagers report seeing it in the distance. It returns to the top half of the corpse before being acquired. The information that helps the reader determine this is revealed in different segments in the description section.

The scientist's observation session, which he commentates for the audio file, involves the scientist explaining that in the last two sessions, it had tried to exit the lab, so for this one, he has evacuated and disinfected the halls to observe what the skip does when it's let out. It blindly but frantically crawls along walls, feeling each doorway before coming to the facility's north exit and being adamant about trying to move through the exit, likely because it can sense the air coming from the outside. After failing to open the door by kicking it, it quickly scurries back to the freezer unit it's kept in and huddles back against its top half, connecting with it like a puzzle piece. As the scientist ends the session and closes the freezer, he hesitates, thinking he saw the top half's arm move, but dismisses it as a trick of light from the leg twitching. As he closes it, a raspy voice whispering, "Need Dad," can be briefly heard as the door is closing (this is not included in the transcript, only the audio file). Since the entity is likely a hive mind, the reader is left to interpret that it is looking for a specific family member, either the baby's father or the mother's father, who probably lived in the village where it was found. The reader will hopefully interpret that the skip was able to transfer some of its neurons to the top half to briefly control the mouth and vocal cords, and when the skip was initially acquired in two pieces, it was probably attempting to do the same thing. So it longs for closure.

The scientist doesn't hear the voice coming from the top half and dismisses the session as only partly informative about what it can do. He keeps the skip frozen to preserve its lifespan until it can be determined if this was a single mutation or something contagious that can happen again. A second addendum reveals that some researchers who listened to the scientist's recording noticed the indiscriminate sound as he closed the door, but the scientist has failed in his attempts to recreate the circumstances that allowed the whisper to be heard. He dismisses it as a noise that he perhaps made involuntarily as he closed the freezer door, thus dooming the skip to be frozen indefinitely.

I hope this is enough to constitute a beginning, middle, and end for a narrative. If you don't agree or don't find it interesting, let me know.

Hey there! I've been interested in doing this for quite some time now, so here goes nothing! :)

► Application info
▼ Application info

Why do you want to be a junior staff on Community Outreach?

I would like to join the Community Outreach Team to help people find their way around the sometimes confusing nature of the Wiki and the SCP Universe itself.

I believe that the SCP Wiki is the most impressive collaborative effort even undertaken by people on the internet - a place born out of passion and pure creativity - and I would like to help make this wonderful thing as good as it can possibly be. I've seen too many people get turned-off on being invested in all stuff-SCP after a couple of moments within the community due to confusion about certain parts of it or just a general feeling of being overwhelmed, and I would love to do my best to prevent that sort of events from happening.

I try to be involved in as many community events as I can - from contests to the Art Exchange - I would love to help to organize such. Bringing this massive community together in new ways that would make people excited for all content SCP-wise would be a dream.

How active are you?

I'm active on-site every single day - although my activity is mostly focused during afternoon and evening hours, I try to keep in touch with the community whenever and however I can. Additionally, I am very active on SCP-related Discord servers, such as Dr. Cimmerian's Discord Server, /r/SCPDeclassified Discord Server, and Site-42 Discord Server - I engage with conversations going on in such almost constantly throughout the day. I try to read and give idea/draft critique on the said platform to every single request I can possibly put in my schedule - anyone who wishes to obtain help in any way related to the SCP Universe or writing for such can find it within my DMs or in the mentioned servers by simply @-ing me.

Additionally, I read a lot. Unless I'm really busy (which doesn't happen very often), I try to read almost every single article showing up on the Newly Created Pages thread. I also check up on the O5 Command forums once in a while to see how staff functions since these topics have always interested me.

Thought most of my activity circles around Discord due to its relative ease in access on both PC and mobile, I also try to reply to as many Idea Critique and Draft Critique as I possibly can on-site and on IRC when I have a free day - though I'm not a frequent user of the second platform, whenever I enter it, I am more than happy to help people with their writing and/or questions about the SCP Universe.

How can we contact you? Wikidot, IRC, and/or Discord?

As mentioned previously, the place I'm most active on is Discord - I go there by Kein#5142; when contacted there, I am going to reply within 1-2 hours unless I'm currently sleeping (my timezone is GMT+1). I will also notice all Wikidot messages since I check any and all sent to me regularly. IRC is not really my thing, so it isn't the most efficient place to contact me, but I will pop-in to check things out there once every couple of days.

Edit: I have heavily familiarized myself with IRC since the creation of this message; throughout the next couple of days, I will be trying to implement it as heavily as Discord into my lifestyle, spending equal amounts of time on both platforms.

If there are any more questions, I would be more than happy to clear things up. Thanks for considering me!

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.
